# `tikv-client-kvproto` native-crate completion audit

This is the atomic completion receipt for the reusable protocol workspace crate.
Its source-of-truth boundary is client-go's shared
`github.com/pingcap/kvproto` dependency at pinned commit
`059694ae4472276644613acccefa24cbc89d959f`, plus the independently pinned
gRPC channelz schema required by client-go's `util/collectors`. The crate owns
one generated Prost/Tonic type identity; `tikv-client` re-exports that exact
identity as `tikv_client::proto` instead of generating or wrapping a second
copy.

## Input and generator closure

The generator closure is complete: 38 top-level schemas are byte-identical to
the pinned kvproto checkout, `proto/grpc_channelz.proto` is byte-identical to
gRPC v1.82.1, and 17 vendored imports provide all transitive schema inputs, for
56 `.proto` inputs total. The separate `tikv-client-proto-build` workspace tool
is the sole writer. It pins protoc 35.1, sorts roots, writes all output to a
temporary directory under `kvproto/src`, installs only after successful
generation, and removes stale Rust/descriptor artifacts. Two clean runs are
required to reproduce the same normalized manifest.

The generated namespace contains all 41 protocol output modules, 977
`prost::Name` implementations, and the descriptor set's 1,029 message
declarations. Both client and server Tonic bindings remain generated. The
crate's only runtime dependencies are `prost 0.13`, `prost-types 0.13`, and
`tonic 0.12`; standalone crate compilation proves that generated code does not
rely on feature unification with `tikv-client`.

## Public contract and consumers

The crate root exposes every generated module and
`FILE_DESCRIPTOR_SET`. Its two unit tests own the pinned wire-tag checks and
the previously missing-family descriptor checks. The root client dependency
edge is ordinary and unconditional. `src/proto.rs` is only a public wildcard
re-export, while `src/logutil.rs` consumes the shared descriptor directly.
`tests/public_proto_tests.rs` compiles as a downstream crate and assigns a
`tikv_client_kvproto::kvrpcpb::Context` directly to
`tikv_client::proto::kvrpcpb::Context`; this is a compile-time proof that the
two paths are the same Rust type, not wire-compatible duplicates.

Inside `tikv-client`, 68 source files consume `crate::proto`; they all resolve
through the one re-export. No generated module imports `tikv-client`, so the
dependency remains acyclic and downstream TiDB/mockstore code may depend on
the protocol crate without depending on the high-level client. The
`publish = false` setting only prevents an accidental crates.io release from
this fork; workspace and Git dependencies can consume the package normally.

## Validation contract

Completion requires exact input identity; two clean deterministic generator
runs; unchanged normalized generated-content and descriptor hashes; crate-only
tests, check, strict Clippy and rustdoc; the no-feature downstream type-identity
test; both complete client library configurations; workspace all-target and
all-feature check/Clippy; doctests; rustfmt; and `git diff --check`, all on
`nightly-2026-08-22`. The final gate results are recorded in the parity ledger
and ExecPlan; live TiKV/PD execution is not required for an ownership-only move
whose generated bytes and public wire types are unchanged.

The final gate satisfies that contract. Two clean generator runs reproduce the
normalized manifest and descriptor hashes above. Crate-only tests pass both
wire/descriptor cases and zero doctests; standalone all-target check, strict
Clippy, and strict rustdoc pass. The no-default-feature external test passes
both public-proto cases. `make check` passes generation, workspace
all-target/all-feature check, rustfmt, and strict Clippy. `make unit-test`
passes 760 no-default workspace tests and 750 all-feature library tests, with
one intentional skip in each matrix. `make doc` passes strict private-item
workspace rustdoc and all 51 client doctests. `git diff --check` is clean.
